lessons.label: Alpha carbons and acidic hydrogens
lessons.title: Alpha carbons and acidic hydrogens
lessons.tag: The conjugate base is resonance stabilized

cards.rule: An alpha carbon is adjacent to a carbonyl carbon. Removing an alpha H gives an enolate stabilized by resonance and inductive withdrawal. For orientation, approximate teaching values are ethanal alpha-H pKa about 17 and acetone about 19; 1,3-dicarbonyl alpha H can be much more acidic. Values depend on substrate, solvent and scale; do not mix pKa tables from different media.
cards.cue: Alpha = one bond from C=O. Carbonyl carbon is not alpha.
cards.trap: Only a site bearing H can be deprotonated there. Stabilization of an enolate explains alpha acidity; do not treat every C–H bond in a carbonyl molecule as equally acidic. Among comparable simple examples, aldehyde alpha H is often more acidic than ketone alpha H. Additional alkyl donation can destabilize the conjugate base; substituents and conditions can change the trend. Aldehydes also often undergo nucleophilic addition more readily than comparable ketones because they are less crowded and less electron-rich.
cards.app: Enolate-like intermediates allow enzymes to make or break carbon–carbon bonds adjacent to carbonyls.

steps.label: 1. Locate alpha sites
steps.text: Pentan-2-one has alpha carbons on both sides of its carbonyl: the terminal methyl and the neighboring methylene.

challenge.explanation: A and C are directly bonded to the carbonyl carbon B.

steps.label: 2. Delocalize charge
steps.text: This oxygen-charged contributor and the carbon-charged contributor in the next step describe one delocalized ethanal enolate. Purple arrows redistribute electrons, not atoms; no proton moves in this resonance operation.

steps.label: 3. Compare the carbon contributor
steps.text: The same atom skeleton now has a carbonyl and a lone pair/negative formal charge on the alpha carbon, shown as H2C−. Both contributors have C2H3O composition and net −1 charge. They are not separate species interconverting in time; the actual ion is delocalized.

rule.title: α-Carbon Acidity (pKa 9–25), Enolate Resonance Hybrid & α-Halogenation / Haloform

items.label: Why α-Hydrogens Are Exceptionally Acidic (pKa ~19–20 vs Alkane ~50)
items.text: Deprotonating the α-carbon creates a resonance-stabilized enolate ion (R–CO–CH₂⁻ ↔ R–C(O⁻)=CH₂) that places negative charge on electronegative oxygen.

items.label: Active Methylene (β-Dicarbonyls, pKa ~9–11)
items.text: A CH₂ flanked by TWO carbonyls delocalizes negative charge over BOTH oxygens, making it acidic enough for complete deprotonation by NaOEt or NaOH.

items.label: Ambident Enolate Reactivity
items.text: Although oxygen holds more negative charge in the hybrid, carbon-electrophiles (R–X, C=O) react predominantly at the α-CARBON to preserve the strong C=O π bond!

comparison: Needs LDA for 100% enolate (RO⁻ gives equilibrium)

figure.caption: Resonance contributors of one enolate, not distinct species or tautomers. Only electron placement differs.

cue.title: Acid-Catalyzed vs. Base-Promoted α-Halogenation & Haloform Test
cue.prompt: Are you halogenating a ketone in ACID or BASE?

items.label: Acid + Br₂ (CH₃COOH / H⁺)
items.text: Proceeds via the enol: adding the first inductive Br atom makes the carbonyl oxygen LESS basic, slowing down the second enolization.

items.label: Base + Excess Br₂/I₂ on Methyl Ketone (R–CO–CH₃)
items.text: Each inductive X makes the remaining α-protons MORE acidic! All 3 α-H atoms are replaced (–CX₃), and HO⁻ cleaves it into carboxylate + yellow CHI₃ precipitate.

items.label: Chiral α-Carbon in Acid or Base
items.outcome: Equilibrates to Racemic Mixture via Planar Enol/Enolate!
items.text: Only stereocenters AT the α-carbon with at least one α-H can racemize; β/γ stereocenters never racemize via enolization.

trap.title: Using Base + Br₂ for Monobromination or Racemizing Non-α Stereocenters

items.label: Common Trap
items.text: Using NaOH + 1 eq Br₂ expecting clean monobromination, or claiming a β-chiral carbon racemizes in base.

items.label: Correct Reasoning
items.text: Base-promoted halogenation accelerates after the first halogen is added (giving polyhalogenation); only α-stereocenters bearing an α-H can racemize via planar enols/enolates.

app.title: Iodoform Test for Methyl Ketones & Thioester Acidity in Acetyl-CoA

items.label: Thioester α-Acidity (Acetyl-CoA)
items.outcome: Thioester α-H Is as Acidic as a Ketone (pKa ~21)
items.text: Sulfur (3p) has poor orbital overlap with carbon (2p), so –SR doesn’t compete with α-carbanion delocalization into C=O!

items.label: Iodoform Diagnostic Test (I₂ / NaOH)
items.outcome: Yellow CHI₃ Precipitate = Methyl Ketone (or Ethanol / CH₃CH(OH)R)
items.text: Secondary methyl alcohols (CH₃CH(OH)R) are oxidized in situ by I₂ to methyl ketones and also give a positive yellow precipitate.

items.label: Triose Phosphate Isomerase (TIM)
items.text: Active-site Glu base abstracts an α-proton to isomerize a ketose phosphate into an aldose phosphate.

cards.rule: Keto and enol forms are constitutional isomers that differ in H placement and a double bond; interconversion requires proton transfer. An enolate is the deprotonated species, not another neutral tautomer. Bulky strong base at low temperature under irreversible conditions often favors the less substituted kinetic enolate. Reversible conditions often favor the more substituted thermodynamic enolate.
cards.cue: Tautomers move H and pi bonds. Resonance moves only electrons.
cards.trap: Kinetic/thermodynamic predictions require the substrate and conditions. More substituted is not a universal stability rule for every enolate. Simple aldehydes and ketones usually favor the keto form, but conjugation and aromaticity can change that. Enolization makes an alpha center planar and can erase its configuration. Reprotonation from either face can racemize a single alpha stereocenter in an otherwise achiral environment; with other stereocenters it can cause epimerization. Rate and extent depend on conditions, so rapid complete racemization is not automatic.
cards.app: Selective enolate generation lets a synthesis control which alpha carbon forms a new bond.

steps.label: 1. Keto vs. enol
steps.text: Ethanal and ethenol have the same formula but different H and bond placement. This enol has OH directly attached to an alkene carbon.

steps.label: 2. Kinetic site
steps.text: For pentan-2-one, bulky LDA under typical low-temperature kinetic conditions often removes an H from the less hindered methyl side.

steps.label: 3. Thermodynamic site
steps.text: Under suitable reversible conditions, the more substituted enolate from the methylene side is often favored. State the conditions before predicting selectivity.

rule.title: Keto–Enol Tautomerism vs. Resonance & Kinetic vs. Thermodynamic Enolate Control

items.label: Tautomers Are Constitutional Isomers (NOT Resonance Contributors!)
items.text: Tautomerism moves a PROTON (α-H ↔ O–H) and shifts a π bond (⇌ equilibrium arrow); resonance moves ONLY electrons with all nuclei fixed (↔ double-headed arrow).

items.label: Why Keto Usually Dominates Over Enol (>99%)
items.text: The sum of bond energies for C=O + C–H is ~45–60 kJ/mol stronger than C=C + O–H. Exceptions: phenol (aromaticity!) and 1,3-diketones (conjugated + intramolecular H-bond!).

items.label: Kinetic vs. Thermodynamic Enolate Regioselectivity
items.text: Unsymmetrical ketones (2-methylcyclohexanone) give the LESS substituted enolate with bulky LDA at −78 °C (kinetic) and the MORE substituted enolate with NaOEt at 25 °C (thermodynamic).

comparison: Keto heavily favored (C=O + C–H stronger than C=C + O–H)
Deprotonates LESS hindered α-C (fastest rate, lower Ea)
Forms MORE substituted C=C double bond (lowest energy)

figure.caption: Illustrative enol structure. Tautomerization changes H and pi-bond placement; resonance does not move atoms.

cue.title: Kinetic vs. Thermodynamic Enolate Reaction Conditions Selector
cue.prompt: Look at the base, solvent, and temperature over the reaction arrow:

items.label: LDA (Lithium Diisopropylamide), THF, −78 °C
items.text: Hindered strong base plucks the most sterically accessible α-H irreversibly at −78 °C before equilibration can occur.

items.label: NaOEt / EtOH or KH, Room Temp / Heat (25 °C)
items.text: Reversible proton transfer allows equilibration to the more alkyl-substituted, lower-energy internal C=C enolate.

items.label: Phenol or 2,4-Pentanedione (β-Diketone)
items.text: Phenol is ~100% enol to preserve aromaticity; β-diketones favor the enol via conjugation + a 6-membered intramolecular H-bond ring.

trap.title: Calling Keto and Enol "Resonance Structures" or Using ↔ Instead of ⇌

items.label: Common Trap
items.text: Saying "acetone is stabilized by keto-enol resonance" or drawing a double-headed resonance arrow ↔ between a ketone and its enol.

items.label: Correct Reasoning
items.text: Keto and enol forms have different H atom connectivity (constitutional isomers that can be observed separately in NMR); Enolate anions are resonance hybrids!

app.title: Pyruvate Kinase Driving Force, DNA Base Tautomer Mutations & Deuterium Exchange

items.label: Phosphoenolpyruvate (PEP) → Pyruvate
items.outcome: Locked Enol Phosphate Tautomerizes to Ketone (ΔG°′ = −62 kJ/mol)
items.text: PEP is trapped in the high-energy enol form; hydrolysis releases the enol, which tautomerizes to pyruvate and drives ATP synthesis!

items.label: α-Deuterium Exchange in D₂O / OD⁻
items.outcome: Replaces All Enolizable α-Protons with D
items.text: Measuring how many H atoms are replaced by D in D₂O/NaOD (via MS Δm/z) reveals the exact number of α-hydrogens!

items.label: DNA Base Rare Tautomers
items.outcome: Imino / Enol Tautomers Cause Point Mutations
items.text: Transient keto→enol or amino→imino tautomerization alters H-bond donor/acceptor patterns during DNA replication.

lessons.label: Aldol addition, condensation, and retro-aldol
lessons.title: Aldol addition, condensation, and retro-aldol
lessons.tag: New bond: donor alpha C to acceptor carbonyl C

cards.rule: An enolate adds to another carbonyl and is protonated to give a beta-hydroxy aldehyde or ketone: aldol addition. Subsequent dehydration gives an alpha,beta-unsaturated carbonyl: aldol condensation. Retro-aldol cleavage breaks the alpha–beta C–C bond of a beta-hydroxy carbonyl.
cards.cue: Addition adds the partner. Condensation also loses water. The new OH is beta to the retained carbonyl.
cards.trap: Aldol products need not contain an aldehyde: ketone donors/acceptors can give beta-hydroxy ketones. Mixed aldols may give mixtures unless donor/acceptor roles are controlled.
cards.app: Aldolase cleavage of carbon skeletons uses this bond logic in metabolism, with enzyme-specific catalysis.

steps.label: 1. Addition product
steps.text: Two ethanal units can form 3-hydroxybutanal. The donor retains its carbonyl; the acceptor carbonyl becomes the beta-OH carbon. The newly formed bond joins C2 and C3.

steps.label: 2. Dehydrate
steps.text: Loss of water from the alpha/beta region gives a conjugated C=C–C=O system. The diagram specifies connectivity only, not an E/Z assignment.

steps.label: 3. Reverse the carbon–carbon step
steps.text: In a retro-aldol, cleave the bond between alpha and beta carbons of the beta-hydroxy carbonyl; regenerate carbonyl-containing fragments.

rule.title: Aldol Addition (β-Hydroxy Carbonyl), Dehydration Condensation (α,β-Enone) & Retro-Aldol

items.label: Step 1: Nucleophilic Addition (Cα Attacks Partner C=O)
items.text: An α-enolate (or enol in acid) attacks an electrophilic carbonyl carbon to form a new Cα–Cβ bond and a β-hydroxy aldehyde/ketone ("ald-ol").

items.label: Step 2: Dehydration to α,β-Unsaturated Carbonyl (Heat Δ)
items.text: Warming in base (E1cb via enolate expulsion of HO⁻) or acid eliminates H₂O to form a conjugated C=C–C=O system.

items.label: Crossed Aldol & Intramolecular Aldol Ring Size
items.text: Clean crossed aldols use one partner with NO α-H (benzaldehyde, formaldehyde) OR pre-form a directed kinetic enolate with LDA at −78 °C. Intramolecular aldols favor 5- and 6-membered rings.

comparison: Forms new Cα–Cβ σ bond (100% atom economy)
Driven by conjugated C=C–C=O π system

figure.caption: Suitable dehydration removes water from a beta-hydroxy carbonyl to give an unsaturated carbonyl; schematic net pathway.

cue.title: 3-Step Retro-Aldol Disconnection Trick for Any Exam Structure
cue.prompt: How do you find the starting carbonyls of an aldol product?

items.label: 1. Label the Carbonyl Reference
items.outcome: C=O Is Reference → Adjacent = α → Next = β
items.text: In a valid aldol product, the β-carbon MUST bear either an –OH group (addition) or a C=C double bond to α (condensation).

items.label: 2. Break the Cα–Cβ Bond
items.outcome: Cut Straight Through the α–β Bond
items.text: The α-carbon piece was the NUCLEOPHILIC enolate; the β-carbon piece was the ELECTROPHILIC carbonyl partner.

items.label: 3. Restore the Original Functional Groups
items.outcome: α-Carbon Gets H (or H₂); β-Carbon Becomes C=O!
items.text: Convert the β–OH (or β=α alkene) back into a C=O double bond to reveal the two starting aldehydes/ketones!

trap.title: Drawing a γ-Hydroxy Carbonyl or Forgetting Why HO⁻ Can Leave in E1cb Dehydration

items.label: Common Trap
items.text: Connecting the carbonyl carbon or β-carbon instead of the α-carbon, or claiming HO⁻ can never leave under any circumstances.

items.label: Correct Reasoning
items.text: Aldol ALWAYS forms a 1,3-functionalized (β-hydroxy or α,β-unsaturated) product; in E1cb dehydration, a stabilized α-enolate pushes out HO⁻ to gain C=C–C=O conjugation!

app.title: Glycolysis Aldolase (FBP ⇌ DHAP + GAP) & Citrate Synthase / PLP

items.label: Fructose-1,6-Bisphosphate Aldolase
items.text: Cleaves the C3–C4 (α–β) bond of fructose-1,6-bisphosphate into DHAP (enamine/enolate donor) and GAP (aldehyde acceptor).

items.label: Class I vs. Class II Aldolases
items.outcome: Schiff Base Enamine (Lys) vs. Zn²⁺ Enolate
items.text: Human Class I aldolase forms a protonated Schiff base iminium with Lys to act as an electron sink; bacterial Class II uses a Zn²⁺ cofactor.

items.label: Intramolecular Robinson Annulation
items.text: Fuses a new 6-membered cyclohexenone ring onto an existing ketone scaffold in steroid synthesis.

lessons.label: Conjugate addition and enamine nucleophiles
lessons.title: Conjugate addition and enamine nucleophiles
lessons.tag: An enone has more than one electrophilic site

cards.rule: An alpha,beta-unsaturated carbonyl can undergo direct 1,2-addition at carbonyl carbon or conjugate 1,4-addition at beta carbon. Enolates and enamines can serve as carbon nucleophiles; their selectivity depends on reagent and conditions.
cards.cue: Michael addition: nucleophile bonds to beta carbon, then protonation/tautomerization restores the carbonyl.
cards.trap: Do not label every nucleophile addition to an enone “Michael.” Direct carbonyl attack is 1,2-addition. Enamines are neutral nitrogen analogues used for alpha functionalization, then hydrolyzed back to carbonyls. A suitable imine with an alpha H can tautomerize to an enamine with N–H by proton and double-bond relocation. Relative tautomer stability depends on substitution and conjugation. A tertiary enamine without N–H does not have an ordinary neutral imine tautomer; protonation instead gives an iminium ion.
cards.app: Conjugate acceptors can react with biological nucleophiles; the site of reaction matters for covalent inhibitor design.

steps.label: 1. Locate the conjugated system
steps.text: The carbonyl group is green, its adjacent alpha carbon is red, and the terminal beta carbon is orange. Locate them by their bonds as well as color: alpha is one C–C bond from the carbonyl carbon, beta is two. Aligned p orbitals allow electron delocalization across the alternating bonds.

steps.label: 2. Choose the beta site
steps.text: The beta carbon, now the green focus, is the terminal alkene carbon two C–C bonds from the carbonyl carbon. A Michael-type addition makes a new bond there; protonation of the enolate-like intermediate restores the carbonyl. Green marks the current focus rather than one fixed atom type.

challenge.prompt: Select the beta carbon of this enone.
challenge.explanation: D is two carbon–carbon bonds from the carbonyl carbon B.

rule.title: 1,2-Direct vs. 1,4-Conjugate (Michael) Addition & The Stork Enamine Synthesis

items.label: Two Electrophilic Sites in α,β-Unsaturated Carbonyls
items.text: Resonance (C=C–C=O ↔ ⁺Cβ–Cα=C–O⁻) places δ+ charge on BOTH the carbonyl carbon (1,2-site) and the alkene β-carbon (1,4-site).

items.label: 1,2- vs. 1,4-Regioselectivity (Hard/Irreversible vs. Soft/Reversible)
items.text: Fierce, irreversible nucleophiles (RLi, RMgBr, LiAlH₄) attack the carbonyl C (1,2); softer or stabilized nucleophiles (R₂CuLi, β-dicarbonyl enolates, enamines, thiols, amines) add to the β-carbon (1,4) to preserve the strong C=O bond!

items.label: Michael Addition + Aldol = Robinson Annulation
items.text: 1,4-Michael addition of an enolate to methyl vinyl ketone forms a 1,5-diketone, which cyclizes via intramolecular aldol condensation into a 6-membered cyclohexenone ring.

comparison: Gilman (R₂CuLi), Enolates, Enamines, RSH, R₂NH, CN⁻
Mild, neutral alternative to strong-base enolates

figure.caption: Carbonyl-carbon and beta-carbon focus on the same enone: possible 1,2 versus 1,4 sites, not reaction products.

cue.title: 1,2-Direct vs. 1,4-Conjugate Nucleophile Classifier
cue.prompt: Which nucleophile is reacting with cyclohex-2-en-1-one?

items.label: Organolithium (CH₃Li) or Grignard (RMgBr)
items.text: Highly basic, localized carbanions attack the highest δ+ center (C=O) irreversibly under kinetic control.

items.label: Gilman Reagent (R₂CuLi), Thiol (RSH), or Amine
items.text: Soft nucleophiles add at the β-carbon to form a resonance-stabilized enolate, which tautomerizes to keep the strong C=O π bond!

items.label: Stabilized Enolate (β-Diketone) or Stork Enamine
items.text: Wait: Aldol gives 1,3-functionalized products; Michael conjugate addition ALWAYS gives a 1,5-dicarbonyl spacing!

trap.title: Thinking "1,4-Addition" Leaves the Nucleophile on Oxygen

items.label: Common Trap
items.text: Attaching the nucleophile to Cβ and leaving a permanent substituent on O (or forgetting tautomerization back to C=O).

items.label: Correct Reasoning
items.text: In 1,4-conjugate addition, the nucleophile bonds to Cβ and a proton initially lands on O (forming a 1,4-enol), which immediately tautomerizes to put H on Cα and restore C=O (net 3,4-addition across C=C)!

app.title: Cysteine Covalent Drugs (Ibrutinib), Glutathione Detoxification & Ubiquinone

items.label: Targeted Covalent Kinase Inhibitors
items.text: Drugs like ibrutinib use an α,β-unsaturated amide warhead that undergoes 1,4-thia-Michael addition with a specific cysteine residue.

items.label: Glutathione (GSH) Detoxification
items.text: Glutathione S-transferase catalyzes 1,4-conjugate addition of GSH to toxic α,β-unsaturated aldehydes produced by lipid peroxidation.

items.label: Fumarase in the Citric Acid Cycle
items.text: Adds H₂O stereospecifically across the conjugated double bond of fumarate.
